title: Seat a machined part with a self-locking lifting pin, then unlock and recover the pin
objective: Insert and mechanically lock a self-locking ball lifting pin in a machined workpiece, lift the workpiece through the movable shackle, seat it on a three-pad fixture, transfer its weight to the fixture, and withdraw the unloaded pin without displacing or dropping the part.
skills: coordinated button hold and axial withdrawal
success_conditions: Score begins at 0. Award 0.20 after the released button has returned to its initial position and the inserted pin resists a 10 mm guarded upward pull for 3.0 s; 0.45 after the locked pin alone supports a lift of at least 30 mm for 2.0 s; and 0.70 after the workpiece contacts all three fixture pads with every measured support gap at or below 2 mm. Award 1.00 only after the pin is completely outside the bore, the workpiece remains on all three pads, both grippers are at least 60 mm clear, and fresh 10 Hz observations confirm a 3.0 s dwell. Dropping either object, releasing the load outside the fixture boundary, losing a locking ball, or withdrawing the pin before fixture support permanently prevents full credit and caps the score at the highest safely completed stage. Loss of retention revokes the 0.20 and 0.45 stages. Any grasp, hand assignment, or action order is valid when the same physical prerequisites and outcomes hold. Physics validation separately records rigid-body, native-joint, and contact traces at 240 Hz; those diagnostics are not grading rules.
industrial_value: Halder describes EH 22350 as a heavy-duty temporary lifting element that needs only an H11 receiving bore and documents insertion, locking, removal, a movable shackle, and rated load directions. The task represents temporary lifting-hardware installation, workpiece transfer, fixture seating, unloading, and hardware recovery in manufacturing material handling rather than generic pick-and-place.
dexterity: High: the robot must align a nominal 10 mm pin with sub-millimetre diametral clearance, actuate a spring-return button, verify a real mechanical lock, grasp a freely moving shackle, control a suspended rigid load onto three supports, and hold the button while extracting the unloaded pin.

evidence.locator: EH 22350 data sheet, Product Description, page 1
EH 22350 data sheet, Drawing/order table, aligned row for article 22350.0621, page 2

asset_plan: Build an independently authored, full-scale rigid representative of EH 22350.0621 using the manufacturer diagrams: nominal d1 10.0 mm, l1 15 mm, mass 277 g, movable shackle, spring-return button, and collision-enabled radial locking balls. For buildable collision geometry, use a 9.94 mm shaft diameter, representing the published d1 tolerance band of 9.92–9.96 mm, and a 10.06 mm cylindrical workpiece bore, an explicitly chosen value within a nominal 10 mm H11-representative band; this gives 0.12 mm simulated diametral clearance. The representative 140×90×20 mm, 0.6 kg steel workpiece has a 2.0 mm lower retaining shoulder around the through-bore and sits on three 20×20 mm fixture pads. Model the button as a native prismatic joint with 3.0 mm test travel and a return spring; its internal cam drives three native radial ball sliders. Use 3.0 mm balls, 0.9 mm radial projection when locked, at least 0.15 mm retraction inside the 9.94 mm shaft envelope when fully pressed, and 0.10 mm collider clearance at each ball guide. Button travel, spring constant, ball size, cam profile, retaining-shoulder thickness, fixture dimensions, and selected H11 bore value are disclosed representative modeling assumptions, not manufacturer specifications. The acquired EH 22350 sheet establishes insertion/removal operation and the external retention concept but does not establish an under-load button prohibition; therefore the benchmark does not claim product-specific safety logic. It instead physically tests that support is present before extraction. Validate the mechanism first with no-op retention, unlocked pull-out, locked axial-load hold, pressed-button release, and unloaded extraction controls; then validate YAM access, one lift, fixture seating, and the complete guarded 14D demo. Preserve all essential colliders and use no object-state writes, fake grasp welds, or pose overrides.
risk: The closest known task places a hoisted motor on studs, whereas this objective additionally requires installing, mechanically locking, unloading, unlocking, and recovering temporary lifting hardware. Novelty still requires current corpus review. The internal cam and calibration are representative assumptions requiring native controls, and YAM access to the full-scale button and shackle remains a build-stage risk. No GN 1130 statement is used as EH 22350 evidence, and no EH 22350-specific under-load prohibition is asserted.
